data.description:
**Problem.** The LLM code review process currently produces too many review passes per change, too many false positives, and shows severity inflation (low-impact findings landing as critical/important). Each unnecessary cycle costs tokens and human attention; severity inflation distorts the resolve/defend gate.

**Goal.** Calibrate the reviewer agents and rubric so that, across a stable sample of representative PRs, (a) the number of resolve→re-review cycles is reduced, (b) false-positive rate drops, and (c) severity assignments better reflect real impact — while preserving true positives and not weakening overall code-quality enforcement.

**Approach (to be brainstormed).** Likely involves: tracking review outcomes per cycle, building a labeled corpus of past findings (true positive / false positive / severity-correct / inflated), tuning agent prompts and the rubric against that corpus, and adding a regression test that catches calibration drift.

**Out of scope.** Changing the review pipeline architecture, adding new reviewer dimensions (that's 4911-c7ba), or modifying override mechanics (that's jira-dig-1673).

Created as a North Star placeholder during /dso:prioritize-epics Phase 2; refine via /dso:brainstorm.
data.title: Code review calibration: reduce review passes, false positives, and severity inflation
